Within the broad framework of quantum resource theories, we introduce a universal resource category, encompassing both non-commutativity and non-orthogonality as fundamental resources. A measure of these resources is devised using the concept of relative entropy. These generalized resources exhibit two key traits: they can be broken down into initial states achievable from no resources and states with a maximum level of this resource, both exhibiting monotonic characteristics. These categories exhibit non-classical properties that prohibit cloning and remote transfer. Moreover, we outline practical methods for extracting valuable resources from a starting state through distillation and dilution processes.

We develop a global optimization method for identifying the starting point
that yields the most accurate parameter estimates in a family of stochastic
differential equation-based models, utilizing data from a set of key
statistical metrics. The method is then put to the test in a case study
involving drug interactions with cyclosporine, an immunosuppressant, and
gentamicin, an antibiotic. Our analysis reveals significant variations in
the effect of cyclosporin on pharmacokinetic parameters depending on whether
concentration or AUC is considered, with the former providing a more precise
estimate but not always reflecting biological impact.

We analyze multi-dimensional time series with infinite variance, yielding finite variance for their averaged versions via the CLT for dependent, sequentially correlated series. This involves proving probabilistic laws for dependent series with a dependence decay criterion known as beta-mixing. Our study focuses on a Poisson-driven dimension reduction technique, which we achieve by reducing high-dimensional data to a lower-dimensional structure. To do this, we establish a variance stabilization effect in dependent series and provide a variance expression for their time series. Our analysis is based on the dependence structure of Gamma-subordinated Lévy processes and applies to a broader class of non-stable time series. Our results explain the emergence of non-stable time series behavior even with a finite variance. Our study also reveals that the variance of gamma-subordinated linear stable processes remains constant, which is a crucial difference from other dimension reduction models such as vector-valued Gamma processes and alpha-maxstable processes. Our analysis also reveals the emergence of non-stable time series behavior in certain cases, such as when a gamma-subordinated linear stable process is used as the dimension reduction model.

Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes have a low decoding time complexity but typically have regular check nodes and density-evolution decoding is limited to a check node degree that increases sublinearly with the block length. Conversely, LDPC codes with cyclic structures allow for a time complexity of linear with the block length but have a larger decoding error probability due to increased check node degrees. In contrast, we've found that quantum LDPC code density-evolution with sublinear time complexity can be achieved through a combination of two independent decoders: the first is a standard LDPC decoder with linear operations, and the second is subquadratic in terms of complexity. When both decoders work together, they provide an overall decoding time of linear with the block length. Furthermore, for quantum LDPC codes with quasi-cyclic structures, we've developed a quasi-cyclic decoder that subquadratically decodes in terms of block length. In addition, we've demonstrated that both classical and quantum LDPC codes can be analyzed using sublinear time complexity, offering significant advantages over cyclic codes in terms of decoding speed.

A vertex set S is considered a distance-r controlling set for a graph G if every vertex of G not in S is at a distance of at most r from a vertex in S. We investigate the problem of finding such set for sparse graphs that have high genus. We show that a set controlling distance of 4, though strongly in a general sparse graph with large genus, is not necessarily so in distributed computation. Specifically, our main result involves showing that achieving a distributed distance-r controlling set for any fixed distance r greater than or equal to 3, is not possible to be done efficiently using a constant number of messages in a specific class of high genus graphs. Specifically, our algorithm runs in $2^{O(r \log r)} 2^{O(\sqrt{\log n}}$ rounds. This is an improvement over the previous best known complexity of $\Omega(r)$ rounds required by any constant degree graph. We also show that finding a distance-3 controlling set for any sparse high genus graph is as hard as finding an independent set for any 3-colorable graph. We also propose a new algorithm that computes a distance-3 controlling dominating set in any sparse graph G in $O(\log^2 n)$ rounds. This algorithm, based on a new set of graph properties, achieves an improved bound on the size of S compared to the best known algorithm for general graphs. We also show that achieving a distance-4 controlling set for any sparse graph is relatively easy and can be

We have developed a general theoretical framework for understanding how one-dimensional topological phases connect to zero-dimensional isolated states at their boundaries within disordered systems. This principle applies to all types of topological phases across various dimensions and disorder levels. Focusing on disordered two-dimensional models that exhibit higher-order topological characteristics, we discovered that an effective interaction can be expressed as a dimensionless contact, which correlates with the dimensionless strength of an isolated state. Moreover, we derived a step-by-step process to determine this general coupling constant using one-dimensional topological models and demonstrated its validation in numerical simulations of two-dimensional models with two-dimensional isolated states. These findings offer a solid foundation for analyzing mass-boundary interactions in disordered environments and can aid in interpreting experimental results related to higher-order topological materials.

This study delves into various beyond Standard Model models utilizing SUSY, focusing on LHC data's impact on these models, particularly non-temperamental points in the model's parameter space, where LHC's distinct capabilities can be leveraged to identify potential signals distinct from those in more traditional points.

Our proposed deep learning framework enhances visual insights by leveraging
spatial context from a dataset, utilizing additional training images to improve
comprehension. Traditional deep learning models rely heavily on individual image
analysis, disregarding spatial relationships, which limits their applicability to
ultra-high resolution datasets. Our approach efficiently leverages high-resolution
input by training models with a sufficient number of overlapping sub-regions and
demonstrates the effectiveness of different architectural designs through
experiments on various micro and nano-scale datasets. The framework enables
visualization of high-resolution datasets, optimizing performance by leveraging
high overlap in the sub-regions.

Observations conducted at the SOAR telescope in 2021, employing the PAXmod interferometric system, yielded 117 successful datasets out of 176 attempts. The resulting dataset featured 187 target stars, with 107 previously unobserved and 81 successfully re-observed through a combined effort of 117 observations. The experiment successfully matched and combined 81 targets from the remaining 268 program submissions. The median number of observed stars per program was eight, and the observed stellar separations ranged from 4 to 15 mas, with a median separation of 10 mas. The experiment achieved a contrast precision of 10^-3 to 10^-5, and fractional luminosity measurements ranged from 10^-6 to 10^-2. The experiment successfully detected 22 excess sources with 10 classified as circumstellar disks, and the remaining eight classified as variable or circumstellar.

We've found that the 3D heavenly space chiral algebra has a full set of topological operator descendants that are conformally primary, and their correlation functions have an explicit, closed form expression. Furthermore, we discovered a specific relationship between the full chiral algebra and specific 2D free scalar theories. Additionally, we found an extension of the colour-kinematics equivalence principle to theories derived from the 3D space, and using an extension of the Ward identity for the chiral algebra, we've integrably reformulated the chiral algebra's correlation functions.

A complete study of an explosive event in the sun's lower atmosphere is presented, observed using low-frequency antennas, including the LOFAR telescope. The event occurred within a dense area of the sun's corona, specifically within Coronal Hole URA1, and occurred within a context that typically exhibits low activity levels. The analysis revealed an impulsive rise in X-ray brightness, accompanied by a radio burst at microwave frequencies and a co-located piston surge at metric wavelengths within the sun's lower atmosphere. The energy release triggered a shock wave that propagated along the polar magnetic field lines, driving a piston surge. The event was followed by a radio burst at decimetric wavelengths, characterized by an impulsive rise in flux density and a slow decrease in intensity, and was accompanied by an electron temperature of approximately 100 million Kelvin. The analysis also detected structured emissions at decametric wavelengths, and the shape of the radio spectrum suggests that high-energy particles accelerated by the piston surge interacted with an ambient magnetic field, and a current sheet formed within the magnetic reconnection region. The event was also observed by instruments sensitive to X-rays, and the analysis revealed a mass of approximately 10 to the power of 19 grams, and a piston speed of approximately 1,000 kilometers per second. The event was also observed by instruments sensitive to microwave frequencies, and the analysis revealed a flux density of approximately 10 to the power of 19 joules per second,

In the Standard Model with two Higgs doublets, any deviation in the muon's magnetic moment is accompanied by discrepancies in the number of generations of leptons beyond a single generation. We've established a probability metric to quantify the magnitude of these discrepancies and found it to be robust within this model framework. Our analysis indicates that the $b d g s$ process is the primary source of the observed irregularities and provides a means to differentiate the Higgs alignment regime from the non-aligned state, thereby reducing the model's parameter space. Furthermore, we've computed the probability values for the two Higgs doublet models and a corresponding list of two-loop contributions.

We develop a stochastic equation in a probabilistic form to create a dynamic representation of Wiener processes in Euclidean space. This Euclidean stochastic equation has a connection to stochastic systems in higher-dimensional manifolds through a stochastic factorization approach derived from Wang's work, specifically for certain Brownian motions in Euclidean space. We utilize our Euclidean stochastic equation to address issues related to probabilistic representations of high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic equations with functional coefficients, including stochastic systems with random dynamics representing a whirlpool of Wiener paths, as seen in Wu's work. Specifically, our equation allows for efficient computation by reducing the dimensionality of the probabilistic flow from $d(W)$ to $d_W$, where $d(W)$ is the dimension of the Wiener space and $d_W$ is significantly smaller. This concept has been successfully applied in various fields, including finance, physics, and biology, to tackle numerous problems involving high-dimensional stochastic systems.

The state of field intensity correlations in a system can be described by an entanglement spectrum derived from its transverse mode overlap matrix eigenvectors. These eigenvectors define the mode entanglement entropy, enabling comparison between different systems. A specific application of this concept involves non-Gaussian states produced by photon sampling in different optical configurations. Studies showed that mode entanglement entropy yields unique patterns for each system, distinguishing between them and revealing the presence or absence of photon sampling. Further analysis revealed that mode entanglement entropy exhibits distinct properties in systems with and without normal modes, showing different responses to photon sampling in these environments.

To determine if a candidate remembers a learning event, we analyze short temporal sequences of mouse movements. These sequences are too lengthy for people to recall accurately, but not so long that natural decay in memory doesn't begin to affect them. By using a deep neural network, called the Grounded Skill Network, we can learn these sequences in a way that is intuitive for biological systems and requires minimal data. This network outperforms other models in both remembering and generating sequences, discovering move patterns that match established psychological findings about human and mouse memory. Moreover, the network is efficient in both the number of movement observations needed and the computational time required, making it a practical solution for experiments involving temporal sequences.

Recurrent neural networks, particularly those containing fully interconnected recurrent units, are often employed in scenarios where the current state of a system influences future states.  We examine the complexity of learning in a specific class of hidden Markov models where the state is partially observable, with various possible views generated by the system at each time step.  We discovered that in some instances, even a basic structure of recurrent networks can fail to efficiently learn these models, particularly when the network has very few units.  We identified the key characteristic responsible for this difficulty as the presence of concealed states, which are unobservable states that do not affect the system's view but are only accessible through more complex networks.  We demonstrated that eliminating these concealed states is necessary for efficient learning by the network, and we proposed a method for achieving this in a general setting, although this process may be computationally expensive due to its exponential nature.  We also explored the relationship between concealed states and belief states, which represent an agent's understanding of the system's state based on its past views.  We found that while some simple belief states can still be hidden from simpler networks, others can be effectively unconcealed, allowing for efficient learning, and we illustrated this with an example of a trivial task solvable by an extremely basic network with just two units.

Human action detection using video data is becoming increasingly significant but remains a complex challenge due to the variability of actions and the presence of irrelevant content in videos. Several successful approaches have been proposed, but they heavily rely on precise annotations. To address this issue, we introduce a new weakly-supervised method for detecting multiple instances of repeated actions within videos. Unlike traditional detectors, our proposed graph convolutional network-based model leverages spatial relationships to identify action contexts and employs attention mechanisms to focus on relevant action regions while filtering out background noise. By combining graph neural networks with temporal convolutional networks, our proposed model achieves impressive results on several benchmark datasets for multi-action detection.

The 2021 Image Similarity Challenge brought together a global community of researchers to tackle an ongoing computer vision challenge by focusing on image similarity tasks. The challenge prompted participants to develop more sophisticated deep neural networks capable of handling complex and real-world images, while maintaining high performance in difficult scenarios. Recent advancements are showcased, encompassing the employed models, used training datasets, outcomes of evaluated models, and novel insights gained from the challenge.

This brief document provides a summary of research findings on the long-term behavior of solutions in parabolic partial differential equations, specifically the mean first passage time, boundary layer structures, and homogenization of parameters. The paper presents findings on how various factors, such as the number of dimensions, number of disturbances, and conditions at boundaries, affect these solutions. Additionally, it explores how different parameter regimes lead to metastable states, and how homogenization can be used to understand the behavior of these systems.

The nuclear substance's computation in the presence of a strong magnetic field using the LOCV method has been investigated. Building upon the magnetic field-dependent nuclear wave function derived using the Gogny force, the LOCV energy density formula was derived. Calculations for neutron and proton number densities were performed within the nuclear substance in the magnetic field. Additionally, energy density, in the range of -16 MeV/fm$^3$, and a compressibility constant, cK of 0.085 fm$^2$, were calculated. These results were compared with those in the absence of a magnetic field. Neutrons in the magnetic field were found to be more confined than protons.

The burgeoning field of communication-efficient Federated Learning (FL) has gained traction in recent years, driven by the need to minimize communication costs across diverse platforms. Balancing data privacy requirements with reduced communication costs remains a significant challenge, particularly when implementing secure communication protocols. To address this issue, we present an innovative approach that leverages existing secure communication methods, allowing for differential privacy-compliant FL with minimal communication costs. Our solution involves a two-pronged strategy: first, we develop an algorithm to enhance model utility while adhering to privacy constraints, and second, we design a new communication protocol that leverages existing secure communication technology. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our approach yields substantial improvements over current best practices, achieving privacy compliance with smaller noise levels and more efficient model updates.

A research paper examines how far ultraviolet light affects the upper regions of the A1 star-forming area, where the UV source is primarily predicted to be the A1 cluster. An observational campaign was conducted using Far Ultraviolet Satellites, specifically FUSE and HST. These satellites observed A1 cluster stars, A1 region molecular clouds, and the nearby Taurus region. Observations of A1 cluster stars revealed that the stars emit strong FUV radiation, with mass loss rates consistent with theoretical models. Conversely, observations of the upper Taurus region showed increased 140 nm radiation and decreased 110 nm radiation, indicating the presence of a 20-30 AU thick H I screen. This was confirmed by FUSE observations of the T Tauri star L1425, which showed the presence of a 10-30 AU thick screen. Observations of the Aur-A complex revealed a similar trend, with the Aur cluster contributing a significant portion of the observed flux.

Structured tables effectively consolidate substantial information in a relatively compact format, making PDF documents easily navigable. However, extracting tables from PDF documents poses a substantial challenge due to the diverse and non-standardized formatting options available to document creators, which vary in complexity and style. To address this issue, our approach involves a novel technique for converting the visual components of PDF tables into a set of recognizable, encoded representations that are more amenable to classification. These representations are then integrated with visual features to form a comprehensive, multi-modal representation of each table cell, which facilitates cell content classification using graph neural networks. The resulting cell labels are leveraged to organize the classification output into a table structure that accurately mirrors the original layout. Our method has achieved exceptional table extraction performance, boasting state-of-the-art results on the CORD19G benchmark, which showcases its efficacy in converting unstructured table data into a well-organized format.

This study proposes a model of strategic interaction that incorporates multiple stages of decision analysis, where agents successively consider each other's potential choices at various depths of reasoning. Unlike traditional game theory models, our model does not assume perfect understanding of information or rationality. Instead, we develop a new approach to resolving cyclic patterns of belief by utilizing a dynamic process that unfolds across multiple layers of cognition. Within this framework, we establish a relationship between complex patterns of reasoning and established concepts from game theory, such as best responses. Furthermore, we utilize this relationship to explore scenarios in which traditional concepts like Nash Equilibrium may not be applicable, including a two-stage Cournot competition characterized by dynamically evolving supply and demand conditions.

In the context of a developing nation like Mozambique, accurate and timely census data is vital for informed decision-making by policymakers to foster economic growth and improve citizens' living standards. Unfortunately, traditional census processes are costly and time-consuming due to their reliance on paper surveys collected by trained enumerators in scheduled visits to households. This challenge is being addressed by the development of a Survey Autonomous Population Estimation, or SAPo, system, which leverages geospatial data and machine learning to provide periodic, precise population estimates. By updating existing datasets and leveraging advanced computational techniques, SAPo aims to offer a regular, accurate alternative to traditional censuses, ultimately supporting Mozambique's goal of delivering reliable survey results every five years.

The substantial storage and retrieval time issues of large datasets can be efficiently addressed using query filters that identify subsets of data relevant to the query in question. Researchers have developed Estimated Membership Query filters (EMQF) to improve filtering effectiveness by providing size estimates for queried subsets. We introduce a novel technique for automatically generating collections of EMQF algorithms without requiring any prior knowledge from the user. EMQF is capable of producing large collections that are free from false positives within a reasonable timeframe by leveraging data retrieval and efficient learning methods. By analyzing a range of datasets, we show that our EMQF algorithm surpasses state-of-the-art alternatives in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

A novel recombination technique is presented for converting a spin polarized mixture of atoms into its diatomic molecule counterpart, with potential application to both bosonic and fermionic isotopes. We utilize the energy released from a laser-driven three-body recombination process to couple specific molecular states. We achieve this by carefully selecting non-strange molecular states, which prevents the release of energy and allows the reaction to produce an excited strange molecule state. We demonstrate this concept through two recombination examples, one involving $^6$Li and another involving $^{40}$K.

A novel, multi-scale Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method is introduced for the analysis of multi-phase, fluid-structure interaction problems. The approach integrates an initial conditions generator that separates multi-scale components and employs a spatial partitioning to distinguish between fluid, interface, and background particles. Through a spatial mapping technique that connects these distinct particle types, the simulation captures large-scale fluid behaviors, such as turbulence and vortex formation, while accurately resolving local phenomena, such as fluid-structure interactions. The proposed method demonstrates its effectiveness in the simulation of complex phenomena, including bubble merging, droplet collisions, and rising bubbles interacting with a flexible mesh.

A quantum learning model, which combines quantum mechanics and general machine learning techniques to solve complex optimization problems, has been explored in this research. This quantum model, which differs from traditional learning methods by not being fully unsupervised, has been tested alongside the standard learning approach. Both methods were applied to a combinatorial optimization problem, specifically the maximum clique problem, using superconducting processors from IBM Quantum Systems, which can operate with multiple inputs simultaneously thanks to their multi-photon capabilities.

A recently developed neural network system called FastPitch is capable of generating high-quality Chinese speech. Despite being able to create speech at various pitch levels, it tends to lose the original speaker's timbre. In order to overcome these limitations, we have developed an alternative approach to estimate the pitch contour by integrating a timbre-preserving adjustment factor. By incorporating this factor, our method can maintain the original speaker's timbre even when generating speech at different pitch levels. Additionally, a new configuration has been established for fastspeech, which serves as a comparison baseline for evaluating our approach. Experimentation reveals that using the adjustment factor allows users to effectively control the speech pitch and timbre independently, and that FastPitch A+ demonstrates superior quality when compared to the baseline fastspeech B at both natural and low latencies.

Many successful deep learning approaches for predicting the behavior of cities overlook a key aspect of city dynamics: the interconnectedness between neighboring cities. This interconnection is evident when considering how transportation systems, such as high-speed rail networks, enable cities within regional clusters to influence each other. To address this concern, a novel framework, Hopper, is introduced, employing graph convolution networks to capture multi-hop relationships between distant cities. By analyzing city characteristics and population shifts over extended periods, specifically from 2000 to 2019, Hopper's performance is evaluated against established models like LSTM, GRU, GraphConv, and GRU-GCN, demonstrating its superiority. Furthermore, Hopper achieves a significant 16.5% boost in predicting city growth over large areas and at long time horizons.

Physicists at the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider have carried out a measurement involving $W$ boson decays into electrons or muons in association with a bottom quark pair. This study utilized data collected with a total integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb$^{-1}$ in the 2015 and 2016 runs. By analyzing various event characteristics, researchers were able to decrease background noise from other large strong force processes. This research presented the first direct measurement of a strong force process involving both a $W$ boson and bottom quarks, resulting in a measured cross product of 1.12 pb for the specified final state, consistent with the standard model's predictions. Researchers were also able to measure the mass of the $W$ boson as 80.29 GeV. This measurement, when combined with other similar measurements, has a consistent result with the standard model's theoretical prediction of a 2 standard deviation. This measurement establishes a constraint on the strength of a specific type of interaction between bottom quarks and charged currents, resulting in an upper limit on a specific coupling strength of bottom quarks.

This study introduces an interactive Telepresence Robot Control (TROC) experience where users remotely operate a robot via a camera and microphone, influencing the behavior of other participants. Participants' perceptions of the system are assessed through questionnaires, comparing them to experienced Quality of Experience (QoE) evaluation metrics. The investigation reveals that a range of camera angles, audio clarity, and environmental context can induce different user emotions, particularly irritation. The findings indicate that communication quality, environmental setting, and user personality traits play a crucial role in shaping user satisfaction. The findings have implications for future research and the development of automatic quality assessment methods.

This study introduces hierarchical regression models through the lens of Bayesian multivariate linear models, revealing the natural connections between these accounts. By exploring proper prior specifications, we demonstrate how Bayesian Bayesian analysis can automatically manage multicollinearity, thereby providing a clear link between Bayesian and classical perspectives. Furthermore, by employing numerical simulations, we compare the performance of Bayesian and classical models when dealing with limited sample sizes and a degree of model uncertainty. Our findings indicate that Bayesian modelling excels in such scenarios.

To explore the game of Mafia, a numerical model was developed, which is analogous to the SIR model used in epidemiology. Simulations utilizing this model were run to investigate key aspects of Mafia, including participant outcomes, game dynamics, and effect of player count on result, which in turn shed light on strategic considerations within this game.

The way massive planets grow in a solar system is still not fully understood, and several theories have been proposed to explain the current disk structure seen in some planetary systems. One possible explanation involves the mass of these planets drawing in gas simultaneously from the disk. This process could lead to a split in the gas disk into a ring and an inner disk due to how the gas reacts to the massive planets. This split might then temporarily regulate the speed of the massive planets' growth. As a result, one planet could end up significantly heavier than the other, and the system would look like the gas disks observed in some planetary systems. The way these planets grow in mass would be greatly affected by the timing and duration of the gas accumulation phase.

The electronic band structure in graphene-based single-walled nanotubes dictates whether it's a metal or semiconductor, and an applied electric field could potentially adjust this structure.  However, an intertube bridge, called the pi-pi prime bond, can disrupt electron flow through the nanotubes even under high external pressure.  Our investigation of how lattice vibrations (phonons) affect nanotube electron transfer in an amorphous film of (5,5) graphene nanotubes shows that phonons can overcome the intertube bridge barrier, allowing electrons to flow freely, and that electron flow can be adjusted by adjusting the temperature.  High-resolution electron microscopy shows that nanotubes twist and turn in ways that can facilitate or impede electron flow.  Our findings suggest that highly conductive nanotube films could be created by managing nanotube positioning and adjusting temperature.

Clustering is a fundamental technique in data mining, but traditional methods struggle with high-dimensional data due to the curse of dimensionality and noise present in data sets. Clustering algorithms also face challenges with outliers and missing information. To address these issues, a novel approach called Variable Feature Weighted fuzzy k-Means (VFKM) is introduced, which incorporates an entropy-driven variable weighting technique to adaptively weight features based on their uncertainty. Our proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods, such as Feature Weighted k-Means (FKM) and traditional k-Means, across various datasets, with results supported by the concept of silhouette width. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that VFKM is more effective in handling high-dimensional data and is more robust to noisy data compared to existing algorithms.

Mixture-of-experts, specifically the gradient-download-algorithm (GDE), is a widely used method for parallel training, yet it is prone to bottlenecks due to its reliance on sequential expert evaluation. A recent study demonstrated that the runtime of GDE is dominated by the time taken to download gradients from the central server, making GDE essentially unresponsive until these gradients are downloaded. This issue arises because GDE halts forward propagation until a round-trip-time (RTT) is completed, resulting in a sequential bottleneck. This problem is addressed by a new algorithm called Gradient-upload-download (GUD), which allows forward propagation to begin after the model parameters are downloaded, rather than waiting for gradients to be downloaded. By using GUD, we can achieve significant speedups, up to 50x reduction in runtime, specifically for low-rank MoE models with sparsity rates of 10%, trained on 8 H100 GPUs for 3 days without sacrificing model quality, as evidenced by our experiments on text generation and text classification tasks.

Consider a smooth, connected graph $G$ with a specific type of Jacobian Jacobian${\rm Jac}(G)$ that exhibits symmetry under the action of $-1$. This symmetry leads to an involution operation $\iota$ that splits into two separate actions on subsets of $G$'s chip configurations: those that remain unchanged and those that change when applied by $\iota$. Based on the behavior of these actions, we define two play types in Token firing games played on $G$: symmetric and antisymmetric games. For specific graphs $G$ that meet a rank criterion, the antisymmetric game is found to be finite. Furthermore, for certain graphs with a rank of at most one, the total number of turns in the game can be calculated using the Menger number. When played on a specific type of graph known as a bridge graph, the antisymmetric game is found to be finite, with its duration determined through quadratic forms involving Prym forms.

To assess the maximum bound on global symmetry disruption in quantum gravity, we consider a simple radiative generation of cosmic birefringence. Our analysis reveals that the associated graviton exchange effect is inherently non-local, thereby violating the equivalence principle to a considerable extent. This has the effect of imposing a stringent constraint on the mass scale associated with such a global symmetry, specifically that it must be less than or equal to approximately 10 million times the Planck mass. This constraint is in direct conflict with the expectations of string theory, thereby raising doubts about the possibility of a stringy origin for such a global symmetry.

Our research explores Far Ultraviolet (FUV) imaging of the globular cluster NGC 4147, a bright galaxy in Coma, utilizing four unique UVIT observations spanning from 2013 to 2017. These high-resolution observations, combined with precise photometry, enabled us to generate a highly detailed FUV-H, V/I band main sequence diagram, thereby allowing us to identify and measure the properties of a significant number of blue straggler stars within the cluster. By carefully analyzing the new FUV main sequence data, we were able to determine the characteristics of these BSS, including their positions, widths, and slopes. Our analysis revealed the presence of a distinct FUV extension in the main sequence, which is highly consistent with the presence of early F-type and late A-type BSS, a population previously observed in the V-band but not in FUV. Our research also allowed us to measure the age of NGC 4147, including a notable 10% margin of error, and provided insights into the potential for BSS formation.

A weak form of Bott's b-principle is presented, effectively addressing the problem of the Mumford b_4 conjecture, with this principle being grounded in the study of real analytic Poisson manifolds and their characteristic classes.

Recent studies on transferability in deep learning have identified two pivotal concepts, which posits that pre-trained deep neural networks should perform better on tasks unrelated to their initial training out of pure chance. Transferable features also exhibit the ability to detect patterns across various datasets from the same domain, such as natural images. While these concepts contribute positively to understanding transferability, they require further investigation and refinement. This investigation explores the limitations and implications of these concepts by analyzing the mechanisms behind generalization in transfer learning, and presents an alternative explanation for observed transferable performance.

In various biological and social systems, the speed at which information spreads among network participants is a critical factor. This research explores how the structural properties of networks, specifically the distribution of weak and strong connections, influence the speed of information diffusion. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations that a network's modular organization acts as a barrier to diffusion, maintaining the speed characteristic of sparse networks even in networks with high connectivity. This finding is validated across various random network models and different diffusion processes.

For each minimal surface $M$ in the complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^3$, we define $\delta(M)$ as the smallest amount of area in $M$ isolated from the rest of the surface $M$ when looking at it from certain angles. Our results show that the curvature of $M$ can be uniquely determined by the value of $\delta(M)$, specifically by examining its maximum and minimum rates of change, as well as by whether its minimum rate of change is a rational number.

A theoretical model known as the standard perturbation model offers a simple mathematical approach to analyze the dynamics of a link, using the link's instantaneous state as a perturbation variable. This model's effectiveness in predicting a link's dynamics is largely influenced by its assumptions and does not always hold true. To address this limitation, a new discrete-time version of the standard perturbation model is developed, which is suitable for systems without amplification and operates in a time-domain setting. This new model is implemented using the trapezoidal rule to transform the standard perturbation model's differential equation into a discrete form, which is then applied to the logarithmic gain equation to derive the link delay. To test the model's effectiveness, a software tool called Perturbed Link Dynamics is created to simulate and visualize the dynamic behavior of unamplified links under various conditions, such as different link gains, initial perturbation values, and noise levels.

Mobile devices have become a critical component of modern life, with the Android platform serving as the primary OS for these devices.  The android platform has become a primary target for attackers, with mobile malware posing a significant threat.  This paper examines the advancements in mobile malware, with a focus on the evolution of evasion-assault attacks, with a specific emphasis on Android.  By analyzing how these attacks have developed over time, we aim to understand the implications for modern malware creation and provide valuable insights for future research in this area.

Distributed systems are becoming increasingly complex, driving the need for a
unified distributed orchestration platform. This is particularly true in the case
of blockchain-based distributed ledgers, where various applications have unique
needs and requirements. Existing solutions often lack versatility and can't be
applied across multiple domains. In response, we've developed Ozy, a universal
orchestration framework that streamlines blockchain interactions and enables
seamless implementation of different protocols. By ensuring consistency and
reliability in interactions, our system enhances the scalability and
interoperability of diverse blockchain applications.

Our research demonstrates the presence of an unexpected reentrant 5/2 quantum Hall phase, which occurs in thin bismuth films within a specific range of Landau level coupling. This phenomenon is characterized by a window of disorder strength, which can be adjusted, in which the 5/2 phase reappears after initially vanishing at higher coupling strengths, where the 3/2 and 7/2 quantum Hall phases are more prevalent.

This work challenges the applicability of the Thakurta metric in characterizing a specific class of objects – static, electrically charged solutions derived within the framework of the Poincare-Lemaitre gauge. A concrete counterexample is provided by comparing asymptotic properties and mass functions of the Thakurta solution with those of an alternative model – the self-consistent cosmological black hole (PBH) proposed by Bonnor. A demonstration is given that the PBH mass exhibits a linear relationship to mass in units of the proton, in contrast to the Thakurta model. A significant implication is that the distribution of PBHs throughout the universe is constrained by a specific upper limit derived from LIGO-Virgo observations of binary mergers, a constraint derived by the arXiv:1801.05372 research. Notably, this constraint is independent of the particular black hole model chosen, thereby rendering it applicable to both the Thakurta and Bonnor solutions.

The planet formation process through pebble accumulation, a key mechanism proposed by the star-formation-in-clouds (SFC) model, relies on the gravitational interaction of pebbles within cloud cores. However, pebbles in the cloud cores may be affected by density fluctuations caused by gas turbulence, potentially disrupting the planet formation process. This study aims to investigate the impact of density fluctuations on the pebble accumulation process. We conducted a series of three-dimensional planet formation simulations, incorporating both numerical and statistical methods to assess the effects of density fluctuations. These simulations were divided into two categories: (1) local density changes and (2) cloud core shifts. We found that density fluctuations can have a significant influence on planet formation by altering pebble distribution and density, potentially hindering the pebble accumulation process. These findings suggest that understanding and evaluating density fluctuations is a crucial step in assessing the efficiency of the SFC mechanism in explaining observed planetary systems.

Overparameterized models that exceed the necessary parameters to fit training data, without regularization, experience a shift from empirical risk minimization to a stochastic process. We explore how these overparameterized models utilize available computations to achieve optimal performance. We focus on a limited computation scenario where the model structure is simplified using specific properties of certain data sets, such as exponential decays and single-peaked functions. Under these conditions, we demonstrate the existence of multiple model solutions, with the model trained through stochastic methods performing significantly better than the ideal solution found by optimization algorithms. Our analysis also highlights the non-linear relationship between model performance and the number of model parameters.

We expanded upon previous work by adapting the "all-but-one theorem" originally developed by Kemper and Letikinsky and later improved by Klein and Terraccese, initially for the integers, and later for solvable groups. Our enhancement generalizes to any countable abelian group. Specifically, we proved that if $A$ is a subset of a countable abelian group with sufficient Bohr similarity, and $B$ is a large enough subset of a sumset, then there exists a significant intersection within a coset for some $A$-Bohr structure.

The dial-a-ride issue involves designing optimal routes for vehicle fleets to deliver services to customers with known pick-up and drop-off locations and known service times for each customer. This paper presents a Branch-and-Trim algorithm to solve the RMP, a subproblem of the Set Partitioning issue, which is a major issue in transportation. The algorithm incorporates additional constraints to ensure that routes can be traversed by the fleet. Numerical tests were performed to assess the efficiency of the method, which outperformed previous research by finding better solutions in most cases. The method also successfully found new best solutions for 10 customers and new feasible solutions for 15 customers in a few cases.

This study introduces a multi-modal pretraining approach for simultaneous image and text processing within the e-commerce sector. Our proposed framework, KEMPA (Knowledge Enhanced Multi-modal Pre-training Algorithm), is divided into two stages: pre-training and fine-tuning. In the pre-training phase, we incorporate an additional knowledge-based module to strengthen the capability of existing image and text encoders through extra knowledge recognition. Our proposed knowledge recognition module comprises two sub-modules: a task-oriented auto-prompt module utilizing auto-prompts to accelerate the training of the encoder's query section, and a task-oriented user simulator module simulating user behavior to augment the capabilities of the encoder's projector. Notably, we demonstrate the scalability of the suggested method through successful pre-training using this knowledge recognition module with three publicly e-commerce datasets: Fashion-20, Fashion19S, and DeepFashion2. Our experimental outcomes indicate that the trained KEMPA model achieves substantial performance improvements, boasting 30% higher mAP and 15% higher mAP@10 on three e-commerce datasets, as well as achieving comparable performance to large-scale foundation models in top1-mAP@10, while requiring 67% less GPU memory.

A potential score is currently used to measure the likelihood of progression in Alzheimer's patients. However, there's no direct correlation between this score and progression. As a result, there's a pressing need for a more accurate and reliable prediction system. There's significant interest in utilizing electronic health records to develop more predictive models. This study aimed to create a more precise measurement of a patient's risk of progression. The approach involved using various neural network architectures, including an innovative model called Deep InfoMax. This model combined deep learning and reinforcement learning to identify and learn the complex relationships between interdependent features. The results showed that the Deep InfoMax architecture achieved superior performance compared to other machine learning models when tested on a large and comprehensive dataset.

Building upon Kripke semantics, we propose an innovative interpretation for computational logic, shifting focus from variable assignments to user interactions through an I/O perspective. To facilitate this, we adapt a standard logic language, allowing terms to represent actions and formulas either describe permissible outcomes following an action or the combined effects of consecutive actions. The proposed approach is demonstrated through the application of a recurrent neural network named IORNN. This I/O-based framework has practical applications in analyzing system behaviors and ensuring safety. Notably, empirical results show IORNN outperforms existing safety detection methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

We have developed an advanced theoretical model to investigate the spin-orbit interaction in a correlated metal. This model is based on a kondo lattice model, combining inter-orbital Coulomb repulsion and a many-body interaction involving orbital, spin, and momentum components. A numerical study was performed using a multi-orbital dynamical cluster approximation to investigate the effect of the many-body interaction on the spin-orbit interaction in a correlated metal near the magnetic quantum critical point. This research reveals that the many-body interaction significantly amplifies the spin-orbit interaction beyond its single-particle value when the system approaches the quantum critical point. Additionally, we have found that the enhancement of the spin-orbit interaction can induce a correlated insulating state even when the single-particle band is half-filled, and that the spin-orbit interaction beyond its single-particle value can be experimentally detected through inelastic neutron scattering.

We investigate the metastability of the conformal shadow substance, a solution discovered by Almaraz, Galster, and Nielsen in 2019 for the critical shamardan equation. This equation has a unique radial ground state. The metastable conformal shadow substance was shown to be the limit of a sequence of excited states, each corresponding to a distinct, large nodal domain ground state in the critical shamardan equation. These excited states possess a distinct, outer domain that shares the same profile as the ground state. As the energy of these excited states is monotonically decreasing, we demonstrate that the outer domain remains unchanged. Utilizing an outer domain solution from this monotone sequence, and showing its lower energy than the ground state, we conclude the metastability of the conformal shadow substance.

In AI-powered medical settings, models often need to be evaluated in real-world settings, which may differ from real-world data distributions. This discrepancy poses a significant challenge, as traditional accuracy metrics can be misleading. This paper introduces a more reliable alternative, which utilizes prediction intervals to assess model performance consistently, even when working with imbalanced or diverse real-world datasets. The evaluation framework presented here, based on conformant prediction, can be applied across various real-world scenarios, offering flexibility and adaptability. Furthermore, it offers an essential 'safety net' by allowing healthcare professionals to make informed decisions with uncertain predictions. Through comprehensive experiments, it's demonstrated that this framework outperforms traditional metrics like top-K accuracy and is comparable to semi-supervised methods that rely on labeled data.

Research into small changes in biomolecules has shown that minor alterations in binding affinity can lead to significant variations in biological function. To study such transformations, conformational dynamics simulations are utilized, but a significant challenge remains: the computational time required to simulate these large changes exceeds available resources on standard hardware. To address this limitation, we have developed an efficient method for simifying DNA conformational changes by employing a technique known as stiff base biasing, which significantly accelerates the simulation process by simulating the movement of individual nucleotides at their own timescale. Using this approach, we have demonstrated improved conformational sampling in AT-rich 40 bp DNA sequences using the same computational time as traditional simulation methods using a weaker force constant would allow on a system with 128 central processing units.

The constant entropy compression method developed by Navarro and Munro offers
an innovative way to compress repetitive sequences of symbols, applicable in
several compression scenarios. This innovative method can outperform traditional
arithmetic coding in many cases, but its performance is contingent upon the
accuracy of entropy estimates obtained from finite samples. The ANS entropy
compression, a patented variation first proposed by Gyarmati and Memon, offers
a computationally efficient implementation, albeit with suboptimal performance
for large datasets. This suboptimality stems from the need for a parameter that
must be determined empirically. This paper delves into the compressibility of
repetitive sequences of symbols using the ANS entropy compression method. It also
proposes a solution to address the suboptimality of current implementations by
introducing a universal formula for determining the optimal compression factor,
which closely approximates that of constant entropy compression using PDF trees.

Research on dielectric spectroscopy in cement-based materials is expanding due to its relevance in performance assessment for low-level waste forms, especially in geopolyminerals. This study focuses on understanding dielectric behavior in two key geopolymer types used in cementitious materials. Dielectric measurements were performed over a 10 to 100 MHz frequency range at 20°C and 25°C for fluids with varying ion concentrations (0.1 to 1.0 mol/L NaCl) and different gel types to identify how ion concentration and gel type affect dielectric properties. Dielectric behavior in ion solutions and geopolyminers was analyzed using the Maxwell-Wagner-Sillars polarization theory. Dielectric behavior was found to be influenced by fluid ion concentration, gel type, and particle size. Dielectric properties were found to decrease with increasing ion concentration and gel type. Dielectric behavior in geopolyminers was found to be 2 to 4 times lower than in similar waste-forming silicate gels due to differences in particle size. These findings provide valuable insight into how dielectric properties in waste-forming gels are influenced by ion concentration and gel type.

A recent trend in high-energy collisions is the emergence of multi-particle correlations. Researchers are investigating how this phenomenon can offer insight into the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics, particularly in relation to heavy-flavor particles. A simulation was conducted to study heavy-heavy correlations of charmonium and charm-charm, as well as charmonium-strange, particles in proton-proton collisions. Results indicated non-trivial behavior in heavy-heavy charmonium-phi, charmed-phi correlations at the LHCb energy scale. Additionally, correlations involving kaon-kaon, kaon-photon, and photon-photon pairs were observed. These findings offer valuable data for experimentalists to conduct further research.

Die vorliegende Studie untersucht den Fortschritt beim Bau von militärischen Schwarmdrohnen durch eine Untersuchung aktueller Fachartikel aus den Jahren 2015 bis 2021 mittels Natural Language Processing. Durch eine NLP-basierte Analyse wurde festgestellt, dass sich der Fortschritt primär in den Bereichen Kommunikation, Navigation und Schwarmverhalten entwickelt hat. Die Untersuchung wurde mit Python und dem Transformer-Modell BERT durchgeführt, um wissenschaftliche Papers automatisch auszuwerten und den Fortschrittsschwerpunkte zu ermitteln.

The correlations of absorption lines in quasar spectra at redshifts greater than 0.6 are examined in detail. Specifically, a three-dimensional analysis is conducted, and results are compared to mock spectra. The findings reveal complex features, including monopole and quadrupole behaviors, absorption line counts and depths, as well as the influence of cosmic flow patterns. Due to the rarity of available data, mock spectra are generated to facilitate a more thorough study. The analysis reveals intricate structures, including those resulting from dark matter fluctuations and patterns, and its dependence on Lyman-$\alpha$ features. Quadratic cross-correlation maps are calculated, and their behavior compared to theoretical predictions. The results of this study suggest that future data from large-scale surveys, such as DESI and SDSS-IV, will enable precise measurements to constrain cosmological models.

In this research, we demonstrate a conversion between emittances occurring during a space charge limited process and observe how this transfer is influenced by varying the shape of the beam's energy spectrum. We utilized an X-band radio-frequency source and implemented simulations to analyze how the beam's longitudinal emittance is modified in relation to its transverse emittance after the beam passes through a quadrupole magnet.

This research proposes a novel sliding sequential conditional variational autoencoder model for trajectory forecasting that addresses the limitations of current methods in handling variable durations and dynamic human behaviors. To capture the dynamic relationships between target objects and the observed trajectory, a graph attention mechanism is introduced into the conditional encoder in a sequential manner. To address the issue of long-term trajectory forecasting, a novel recursive decoding mechanism is developed, which variationally updates the posterior distribution over latent variables. Furthermore, to improve long-term performance, a rethinking module is introduced that takes into account human re-planning capabilities and the limitations of current sequential models. By utilizing a sliding window, the proposed model can effectively handle trajectories of various lengths and achieve more accurate trajectory forecasting. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art methods on two public datasets.

A novel approach to measuring the complexity of Boltzmann machines is presented, focusing on information theory-based methods. Two Boltzmann machines are analyzed: a biologically-inspired model by Hahn and Mead and a Siwy model adapted to a hyperbolic cosine energy function. Quantitative measures of global and local extended mutual information are used to characterize data propagation within the network. By comparing the extended measures to the delayed counterparts, the communication dynamics within each network are characterized. A hyperbolic cosine-based Siwy model exhibits lower extended mutual information values than the traditional Bernoulli unit Hahn-Mead model, suggesting a potential for enhanced computational efficiency and information processing capabilities through the Siwy model. The results indicate that Siwy models may possess reduced global memory and local connectivity, yet a higher degree of conditional independence and information processing capabilities, paving the way for novel network architectures.

This study aims to introduce a novel approach to sequential hand motion recognition, enabling swarms of robots to be controlled through a series of hand gestures. We've developed a system to identify multiple hand gestures in real-time by integrating depth images with a long short-term memory network. Our experiment involved creating a dictionary of basic hand gestures and trained the system using a large dataset of synthetic hand data, supplemented by real human data to enhance its generalizability. Additionally, we've implemented a hand tracking system that facilitates real-time communication between humans and a swarm of mobile robots. Our results indicate that our proposed method achieves high accuracy in distinguishing between hand gestures, and our distributed sequence recognition framework demonstrates success in handling timing discrepancies between human and robot processing speeds. Our experiment also highlights the potential of utilizing real hand motion data to improve the adaptability of our system to unstructured environments.

The classification of blood cells is a critical component in diagnosing various diseases.
Full blood examination is the primary method used to identify diseases, but the process is
hindered by the complexity and diversity of blood cells.  The time-consuming nature of
manually categorizing these cells necessitates efficient and accurate automation solutions.
We introduce a novel approach to Cytometry Lymphocyte Classification utilizing a merger of
pre-trained neural networks from the study by Abdulla et al. [1] and Wang et al. [2], which
achieved high accuracy but had conflicting models for certain cell types. Our results show
that combining these models leads to enhanced accuracy and robustness, particularly in the
identification of Neutrophils.  To validate the improved performance, our framework was tested
using datasets from different hospitals and achieved exceptional inter-test consistency.  The
overall accuracy was increased by 1.5%, and the accuracy for Neutrophil classification
achieved nearly a 2% improvement.  The comprehensive accuracy and robustness achieved
demonstrate the potential of the proposed approach for Cytometry Lymphocyte Classification.

Quantum technologies rely heavily on high-fidelity quantum states, but the sophisticated requirements of achieving this often hinder the development of quantum processors. Counterdiabatic driving is a powerful technique that enables systems to reach complex target states from simpler initial states, but it frequently involves complex interactions that are difficult to realize experimentally. By employing a counterdiabatic protocol with a probabilistic outcome and a simplified structure, we can guide models like the Hubbard and optical lattice two-level systems to their ground states, even with adiabaticity and experimental imperfections. Notably, this variance-proposed unitary transformation possesses a simplified local structure consisting of up to four-body spin-tensor products, bringing it closer to experimental feasibility.

The speed of color conversions in typical color management systems is often a significant hindrance, particularly when processing large volumes of image data. The current systems' reliance on the precise calculation of color differences to determine color space transformations is the primary cause of this delay. The color Decolor2RGB algorithm has been developed to overcome this limitation, specifically for applications involving the conversion of grayscale images to color based on hue temperature. The new algorithm leverages an approximate method, eliminating the need for slow color difference calculations, and its performance was evaluated by comparing it to the traditional Decolor2RGB approach. The results indicate that for a specific hue range, the mean squared error between the two methods was under 0.05, and the new algorithm's performance was at least 10 times faster than the traditional method.

We propose a novel exponential Taylor expansion method for estimating functions within finite dimensional manifolds, exhibiting an exponential rate of improvement as the number of data points increases, similar to its performance at pointwise data evaluation. Our analysis of bias is rooted in geometric properties, accounting for the influence of the manifold's curvature, and it is applicable to various data types, including those with noise, missing values, and data projected onto the manifold, as well as points in close proximity to the manifold. Furthermore, our results are utilized to establish performance guarantees for multiple manifold-related machine learning algorithms.

We establish that in a CAT($k$) surface with upper curvature bounds, any map $u$ belonging to the $BV$ class and having a distributional Laplacian supported on a set of finite $\mathcal{H}^{1}$-measure can be represented as a harmonic function outside of that set and is differentiable almost everywhere except on that set. This result is applied to study minimizers of $p$-Laplacean functional for $p>1$ and to investigate the properties of $1$-modulus of families of curves on such surfaces.

The intersection of laser-plasma and photon-photon physics is a highly dynamic field, where laser-plasma interactions can generate intense, polarized x-ray and gamma radiation, enabling scientific breakthroughs in fundamental physics and novel electron acceleration methods. This article reviews the current state of the art in laser acceleration and emission of coherent beams, and explores the potential applications of this technology in physics, including physics reviews - gamma ray sources, electron-positron annihilation, and photon-photon scattering, as well as the properties of matter and nuclear excitations. We also examine the capabilities of existing experimental setups and propose a roadmap for future experiments, along with the technical requirements for building gamma ray sources and the potential scientific breakthroughs they could achieve.

This work examines the responsiveness of the low-energy effective potential operator (LEEPO) $C_4$ at a low-energy scale $\Lambda_{\rm eff} \sim$ TeV to $B$-meson observables at current experimental precision levels within the Two Higgs Doublet Model (2HDM) type Ib framework. It investigates how the 2HDM's soft-breaking parameter $m_{12}$ affects these observables and reveals that in corner regions of the parameter space, $C_4$ can be substantially amplified at the low-energy scale, even when other $C_i$ remain negligible. Notably, the work demonstrates that $C_4$ has a negligible impact on the $\Delta \Gamma_{D_s}$ observable, but a significant influence on $\langle {\cal B}(B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-)\rangle$, where it can introduce deviations from the Standard Model predictions by factors ranging from $\sim 10^{-2}$ to $\sim 10^{2}$. Notably, values of $m_{12}$ that significantly affect $B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ can have minimal influence on $B_D\to\mu^+\mu^-$. This work demonstrates that existing precision measurements on $B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ impose stringent constraints on the 2HDM's parameter space, particularly its $Z_2$-violating parameter $m

The increasing availability of data on the World Wide Web in RDF format has given rise to a diverse range of shape expressions that enforce structural constraints. To facilitate seamless interoperability, data must be translated between relational and RDF systems. In general, this translation process entails two key steps: a relational-to-RDF phase and a schema translation phase. However, when shape expressions are involved, the relational schema must be augmented with corresponding shapes to enable translation. In this paper, we concentrate on translating data into RDF formats that adhere to the OWL2 QL profile, which supports all queries expressible through relational databases. By leveraging existing research findings, we aim to fill a critical knowledge gap and outline the challenges associated with translating data, relations, and properties into RDF formats that incorporate shape expressions.

To effectively explore complex non-parametric data relationships, we need to move beyond traditional convex regression. A new python library for convex regression has been developed to leverage convex functions and their extensions, including boundary estimation, in both one-dimensional and multi-dimensional spaces. This framework can be particularly useful for financial and economic analysis due to its connection with time-series and cross-sectional extrapolation problems. The library's capabilities were showcased using real-world datasets, highlighting their potential in financial and economic research. With a focus on interpretability and precise parameter estimation, this library provides a practical solution for data scientists and economists. The python library 'pyStoNED' has been created to make convex regression models easily accessible and computationally efficient.

Our study presents potential searches for a 125 GeV Higgs boson created alongside a top-pair in the $\phi$ channel at the LHC, where top quarks are produced in pairs along with a single Higgs boson, a process that represents beyond the Standard Model behavior. This search utilizes the most up-to-date calculations for related cross sections and values the difference between them as recommended by HiggsTools, a software tool, at the center energy of 13 TeV. This software tool employs the Effective Field Theory (EFT) framework, a method that allows for flexible exploration of potential new physics scenarios, and focuses on two distinct types of $O'EFT$ scenarios, often referred to as Type A and Type B. Furthermore, our analysis investigates the detectability of the $\phi$ channel at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) for both low and high values of the integrated luminosity, and specifically examines the impact of the EFT parameter space on distinguishing between scenarios.

We explore the application of pre-trained language models (PLMs) in natural
language processing tasks that demand minimal or no human supervision. Our
research includes evaluating the performance of pre-trained models in few-shot
learning and unsupervised settings, where we develop a new baseline for few-shot
classification that outperforms comparable methods, and a simplified framework
for unsupervised learning based on pre-trained models that surpasses existing
unsupervised baselines. Our findings suggest that large pre-trained models can
significantly outperform smaller models in unsupervised and few-shot learning
tasks, and that these pre-trained models can achieve comparable performance to
manually designed features in few-shot learning with significantly less labeled
training data. Our study aims to provide a starting point for future research on
the unsupervised and few-shot learning capabilities of pre-trained language
models.

The accuracy of speech recognition systems heavily relies on availability of language data.  Unfortunately, annotated data, particularly in languages other than German, is often scarce or costly to obtain.  In an effort to address this issue, a large dataset consisting of roughly 400,000 hours of unannotated German speech data is presented alongside research on automatically transcribing unannotated speech texts.  In addition, a modification of the speech recognition data pipeline is introduced that enables efficient processing of unannotated data, and an automated method for annotating speech data is described that makes use of Google's public speech recognition API.  Furthermore, an Open Source speech recognition system is introduced that is capable of producing acceptable results on German speech data after being trained with unverified annotations.  In a corresponding evaluation of speech recognition accuracy, it is observed that a system trained on a subset of roughly 70,000 hours of unannotated German speech, and subsequently verified by humans, achieves comparable accuracy to a system trained on a publicly available annotated dataset known as the CTW corpus.  In fact, human evaluation rates the quality of speech data produced by the smaller training dataset as slightly better.  Importantly, it is noted that the knowledge gained from training on unannotated texts is substantially more cost-efficient to obtain than the knowledge gained from annotated texts.

The 30 Doradus nebula, located within the Large Magellanic Cloud, is home to a striking collection of 87 HII regions. This complex is home to 30 Doradus A, the largest and most luminous HII region, characterized by 30 Doradus O-RII stars.  We conducted a detailed spectroscopic analysis of 11 Be-type stars located within 30 Doradus A, utilizing high-resolution and high signal-to-noise optical spectra.  This analysis revealed that the stars are spread across a broad range of spectral types, spanning from O7.5 to O9.5.  Spectroscopic examination of C IV, O VI, and HeII emission lines indicated the presence of Be in all 30 Doradus A-Be stars.  Utilizing the OBStar software, we calculated the ages of the stars, which ranged from approximately 1.5 to 10 million years.  Three of these stars, however, appeared to be older, estimated to be around 15 million years.  Our study of these 30 Doradus A-Be stars revealed a broad range of mass-loss rates, spanning from approximately $10^{-7}$ to $10^{-4}$ solar masses per year.
