This paper presents a text classification approach called Sibylvariant classification, focusing on robustness as the key metric of evaluation. A Sibylvariant classifier, designed to withstand various forms of noise and anomalies in the test data, is applied to the 20 Newsgroups dataset to showcase its efficacy. A large margin loss function is employed, coupled with adaptive training data selection to identify inauthentic samples. Notably, the classifier outperforms competing methods by consistently achieving a lower average loss and a higher accuracy rate on 20 Newsgroups, with its accuracy rate being 79.71% compared to 79.63% for a kernel SVM, as demonstrated through experimental results.

We present an innovative approach that teaches neural networks with small children through simple visual demonstrations. This demo system, inspired by the idea of teaching by example, allows us to effectively train neural networks despite using limited data sets. In doing so, we address a key challenge in computer vision by bridging the gap between abstract network-internal representations and tangible visual forms that can be easily understood. Our method, utilizing visual free-energy, enables the visualization of abstract network-internal representations, leading to improved visual object classification, particularly for children. Notably, the successful integration of this visual demonstration into the entire training pipeline necessitates the assumption that our network's visual representations are demonstrable to humans, which we verify by conducting an experiment with children. By leveraging this feedback, our system automatically enhances the learning process by using simple visual forms as a guide.

In our research, we investigate the effects of knowledge distillation and parameter sparing on multilingual machine learning models. The experiment, which examines knowledge distillation and a novel sparsification technique utilizing quantization, aims to identify whether these techniques can be used to produce lightweight machine learning models that are robust to their own compression. The results indicate that quantization has a higher potential of producing stable lightweight models, outperforming parametric sparing techniques.

By developing hypergraph transformations that preserve hypergraph solitons and analyzing their infinitesimal forms, a novel non-linear and non-degenerate hypergraph Laplacian is discovered, which leads to a solitary hypergraph field equation. This field equation can be derived from a Lagrangian density, with the defining characteristic being its non-predicative nature.

In recent years, deep learning techniques have gained significant attention in the medical image segmentation field. However, these approaches typically necessitate substantial amounts of annotated medical images and advanced, highly tuned architectures. As a result, they are often impractical for real-world applications due to the high cost of gathering and labeling medical data. To overcome these challenges, a more end-to-end approach has been developed, which employs unsupervised image-to-image translation methods to reduce the reliance on annotated data and enhance the accuracy of segmentation. Our research investigates whether image enhancement can aid pneumonia segmentation without compromising the overall performance of this technique. We evaluate various enhancement operators, including those that improve the quality of chest X-ray images, and compare their effectiveness against a baseline dataset. Our results demonstrate that incorporating image enhancement can lead to substantial reductions in the size of the training dataset required for accurate segmentation, as well as significant improvements in the quality of generated images using the Vagan editor, which achieved the best results, including a PSNR of 5.22 and a MSE of 0.006.

In real-world settings, AI systems should be able to adapt their behavior according to the needs of different users. This should include capacity to modify their behavior in a diverse range of ways. For instance, an image description system should be able to generate concise or detailed descriptions according to a given constraint. This concept is known as controllability, and it is crucial for AI systems to have this capability. This paper proposes a method that leverages a large language model's inherent capabilities to generate images with specific characteristics, and it demonstrates an image description task that requires the generated descriptions to adhere to given constraints. The method's effectiveness is evaluated through both qualitative and quantitative assessments, and it is shown to have a range of desirable properties.

This paper explores the etymological and etymologically-informed theoretical
development of the concept of causality from damage, drawing on common German
scholarship. However, it critically examines and challenges the interpretation
of key words, particularly 'Kausalit\"at', based on its etymological insights.
The study also discusses potential future research directions in the area of
causality research.

This study introduces a deep learning framework specifically designed for large-scale applications leveraging Spark and Python capabilities. The framework prioritizes flexibility and is built to accommodate various neural network architectures and be easily enhanced with new features. It is implementable within Flink and MLlib subprojects of the Apache Software Foundation and was developed collaboratively through contributions from multiple developers. The framework was tested using real-world datasets, and a particular emphasis was placed on its ability to handle semi-supervised learning tasks. The study concludes with a detailed overview of key concepts and design considerations for deep learning framework development using Spark's machine learning tools.

Our research explores the field of Zero-shot Voice Translation, which involves 
translating voices from languages never seen before during the training phase. 
We introduce two Zero-shot Voice Translation models, which demonstrate 
significant results on their respective tasks. The first VTT model, based on 
pre-trained acoustic and linguistic representations, shows successful 
translation in both visible and invisible languages. The second VTT model, also 
pre-trained, utilizes a speaker encoder for representational language 
extension and further integration with the first model's neural speaker 
modeling for representational integration. Our proposed system outperforms the 
baseline system in terms of intelligibility and similarity across multiple 
languages, achieving even greater success in translating visible languages, 
furthermore it even excels on the TED-LSMT corpus.

We examine the existence and uniqueness of a solution to a system of partial differential equations derived from a model introduced by G. A. Maugin and J. L. Vazquez, with a focus on materials adhering to the flux law and subject to spatially varying dynamic constraints within a bounded domain extending into time. Under the assumption that the energy functional's second derivative is non-positive, a unique solution to this system can be determined through a differentiability approach. Notably, the validity of our results relies on a condition involving the surface heat exchange coefficient's magnitude relative to the inertia coefficient, effectively ensuring the surface heat exchange coefficient's invertibility.

The integration of renewable energy technologies and electric mobility in domestic settings poses significant challenges to predicting low-voltage grid load. To address this, a statistical analysis was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of combining forecasts from multiple models, which outperformed any single model alone, especially when predicting daily peak loads on a day-ahead basis. Moreover, it was observed that stochastic models outperformed their deterministic counterparts when adjusted for coverage probabilities, albeit at the expense of increased computational complexity.

The increasing popularity of AI technology has led to numerous AI models being developed across various fields. However, domain-specific knowledge integration remains a significant challenge, despite the potential benefits of expert systems and knowledge graphs in facilitating expert knowledge contribution. This paper presents a systematic approach to incorporating domain expertise into machine learning models, drawing on insights from literature reviews and use-case analysis. By doing so, this study aims to guide future research in natural language processing and beyond. Ultimately, this paper seeks to answer the question of how to effectively integrate domain expertise into AI models.

The COVID-19 pandemic presents significant challenges to the healthcare industry, with many patients suffering from prolonged symptoms, a condition known as "Long COVID." To better understand this phenomenon, researchers are using brain imaging to identify distinctive features associated with post-COVID patients. However, biases in training data can skew the results of AI-based analysis. To address this issue, we propose a novel machine learning framework, COLD, that minimizes the effects of biases by employing computational topology and adversarial learning techniques. Our approach outperforms state-of-the-art models by a significant margin in models, accuracy, and Dice scores, and also demonstrates robustness against biases by testing with data from diverse hospitals.

The automated localization and identification of vertebral bodies in CT scans is a fundamental step in spinal disease diagnosis. However, achieving highly accurate results solely through deep learning-based methods proves challenging. This paper proposes a novel two-stage rectification and CSPN generation framework, designed to enhance the accuracy of vertebral localization and identification. We leverage the efficacy of Spine-Nets and anatomically constrained optimization to improve CSPN localization and identification capabilities. Our approach first utilizes a hybrid Spine-Net to correct vertebral positions, compensating for inaccuracies in purely deep learning-based vertebral localization. We then integrate deep learning and anatomically constrained optimization to produce high-quality CSPNs. Our method has been extensively evaluated using the public LEVIR-20 dataset and comparison experiments. Our results show that vertebral localization using the hybrid Spine-Net, combined with an anatomically constrained optimization-based CSPN generation module, significantly outperforms state-of-the-art CSPN generation methods and achieves a 10.1% improvement in identification accuracy over state-of-the-art identification methods. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed framework surpass those of comparable vertebral localization and identification methods, with potential for real-time clinical application.

Our study investigates the scattering of high-energy electrons by an oscillating two-level atom system in the ultrastrong coupling range, employing the Jaynes-Cummings model based on Dirac's dynamic dipole theory. We find that vacuum light atom interactions lead to a significant suppression of the atom's excitation after the electron passes through, effectively 'quenching' the atom's excitation and stabilizing it by disrupting the light atom dynamics. This quenching effect is observed through oscillations in the atom's excitation probability that are phase-locked with the electron's trajectory and exhibits resonance characteristics. We identify two coexisting quenching mechanisms arising from distinct, concurrent quenching pathways that can be coherently combined, giving rise to resonant quenching phenomena. Our results reveal that at a specific quenching resonance frequency, the amplitude of the atom's excitation probability oscillations significantly increases, potentially reaching a 50% difference between its maximum and minimum values. Our findings demonstrate a significant and controllable quenching of an atom's excited state by an electron through vacuum light atom interactions in the ultrastrong coupling range, offering new possibilities for manipulating atomic and cavity states on a very short timescale.

A cutting-edge type of quadruped robot features elastic-driven legs that enable a significant decrease in mass and enhance actuation efficiency through the strategic use of passive dynamics. Nevertheless, implementing this technology poses a substantial challenge for learning-based approaches, primarily due to the inherent variability of the system's dynamics caused by the integration of passive components. This paper introduces a groundbreaking elastic-legged quadruped robot and presents a novel model-based control strategy that integrates planned leg deformations to maintain stable locomotion on uneven terrain. In contrast to conventional elastic-legged robots that neglect leg elasticity, this innovative design maximizes actuator potential to adapt to unpredictable changes in terrain and self-generated forces. We further propose a novel deep reinforcement learning framework, specifically designed for training quadruped robots equipped with elastic actuators, which successfully adapts to diverse terrains and self-imposed disturbances. The proposed method demonstrates remarkable terrain generalization capabilities in simulated environments, including level terrain, random obstacles, and sloped surfaces.

We develop a novel approximation technique for computing the distinguishability of highly entangled quantum states, encompassing both matrix and operator algebraic tools. This method can effectively handle states that are only slightly perturbed from a reference state and demonstrates capacity to address a broad class of sophisticated quantum states. As an illustration, our method is employed to tackle the distinguishability of particle interferometer states affected by dephasing noise. We show that our approach can accurately model complex interference patterns resulting from subtle perturbations to interfering quantum states.

This study provides a rigorous examination of a small-scale reconnection phenomenon in the collisionless regime, specifically within a two-dimensional error function-shaped magnetic structure. Utilizing a self-consistent Vlasov-Maxwell approach in a particle simulation, researchers explored the effects of increasing magnetic shear on the current sheet's instability, exploring three distinct scenarios of plasma response. These scenarios encompassed a fundamental electron hole formation and ion electron separation at its endpoints, leading to magnetic reconnection, up to magnetic shear dominated instabilities that reposition electron holes to both ends of the current sheet. Furthermore, researchers investigated the impact of electron holes on the global electron distribution, observing the emergence of a bi-modal distribution characterized by two distinct populations moving in opposite directions. As a result, strong electron currents form at the endpoints of the current sheet, triggering a secondary electron hole and giving rise to a magnetic island. Subsequently, researchers explored the influence of this island on the global system, including the emergence of whistler waves and the onset of a stochastic regime within the electron hole region. Utilizing a self-consistent approach, researchers were able to accurately reproduce these effects at the kinetic scale, thereby validating previous hybrid simulation results that employed more simplified models for electrons and ions. Lastly, researchers compared their findings to a theoretical model developed by Schindler et al., demonstrating a qualitative agreement between the two.

Fashion image retrieval using raw pixels is a complex task.  The challenge is
due to variations caused by factors such as pose, lighting, and camera angle,
as well as manipulations like cropping, blurring, and filters, all of which affect
the fashion attributes being searched for. To address this issue, we introduce
a method that extracts and incorporates high-level, semi-supervised features
into a model trained on raw pixels, using feature manipulation to group images
with similar characteristics in the embedding space. Our approach includes two
methods for feature extraction, feature enhancement, and attribute-weighted
loss to group query and database fashion images according to their attributes.
We evaluate our approach on the FST50 benchmark and achieve state-of-the-art
performance in both raw pixel and unnormalized image retrieval scenarios.

The dual gradient descent method is developed to address the challenges of linear ill-posed problems in Banach spaces. It's proven that the dual gradient approach generates a family of regularized approximations associated with a dual regularizing parameter, which, under the condition of the source type, converge weakly to the true solution as the parameter increases without bound. The rate of this convergence is determined by both the selection of the dual regularizing parameter and the degree of smoothness of the true solution. Optimal results are achieved when a particular balance is struck between these two factors. Additionally, it's established that a balanced choice of the dual regularizing parameter leads to stable dual regularizing effects. As a practical application, the method is used to analyze the Cauchy problem for elliptic equations on three-dimensional boundaries.

Depth estimation from light field data is crucial for a range of applications, 
including enhancing 3D light field displays, object segmentation, and occlusion-aware light field rendering.
Our novel approach adds realism to synthetic light field renderings by incorporating occluded areas and refines 
depth calculations from data with visible neural radiance fields using an improved active contour model.
The method's effectiveness in both creating realistic synthetic data and improving depth calculations 
is verified through experiments utilizing commercial superlight boxes and real-world datasets.
The approach utilizing the bilinear method to derive the Fokas-Lenells equation, along with its associated spectral problem, is presented in this investigation.

Our specific choices of double Lagrangians lead to actions that correspond to non-Riemannian geometries, similar to those resulting from particular group manifold formulations in double field theory. These actions can be seen as specialized instances of a universal double YM action, although this action has a problem due to its complete gauge symmetry leading to an over-abundance of constraints that render the action non-propagating. To overcome this issue, we also investigate the Higgsed counterparts of these theories, similar to how the DFR action was derived. Notably, we discovered that a particular non-Riemannian double Lagrangian we selected has a gauge symmetry set that differs from those associated with other theories we studied, thereby distinguishing it from the DFR model.

In order to improve the efficiency of wireless networks, we have developed a new method for automatically selecting access points based on channel load using the un reliable Option D of the IEEE 802.11v standard. Channel load information, provided by access points, allows clients to determine the most suitable target access point for roaming, minimizing the need for trial and error and reducing the negative impact of contention, interference, and collision on network performance. Although Option D enables roaming without reassociating with an access point, we found that the current implementation in wireless drivers is insufficient. Therefore, we have modified the Linux wireless driver to utilize the option D mechanism, combined with the IEEE 802.11k and 802.11r standards, to achieve faster and more efficient roaming between access points. Our approach, implemented in a testbed environment, successfully minimizes unnecessary access point switching and improves network performance and user experience when moving within a network coverage area.
